clue.text: Face repair after use

definitions.note: plural answer read as the collective look of a face

indicators.note: to repair something is to put it back together in a new working order

parts.note: both words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone needs a facial touch-up once they have been put to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Your features are the parts making up your face, so the word stands for the face as a whole.

clue.text: Hurt? Get something from pharmacy

indicators.note: taking something out of a word means a run of its letters is lifted out

parts.note: letters two to five of the word

explanation.surface: Someone in pain wonders whether to pick up a remedy at the chemist.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurt someone and to harm them are synonyms, both meaning to cause injury.

clue.text: Responsibility for bird

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as in 'that's not my ...', one's own concern
second meaning: the common town bird

explanation.surface: Someone is put in charge of looking after a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not my pigeon' is a British idiom for 'not my business', which gives the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an idiomatic term for one's own affair or duty and the name of a familiar grey bird.

clue.text: Charlie, not Mike, at front of wedding coach

indicators.note: one letter is put in place of another, so the second named letter is dropped for the first

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
Mike is M in the NATO alphabet
a wedding is a marriage ceremony

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie, rather than one called Mike, rides up front in the wedding car.
explanation.walkthrough: MARRIAGE loses its opening M and takes C instead, giving CARRIAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A carriage is a horse-drawn coach, or a railway coach.

clue.text: Given duty, sort of chef is up and working

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a commis chef is a junior kitchen chef
the word read upwards
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A junior cook has been assigned a shift and is busy at it.
explanation.walkthrough: A commis chef is the lowest-ranking cook in a professional kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission is a task or assignment entrusted to someone, a duty they have been given.

clue.text: Pressed, I must accompany two guys

parts.note: taken as written
two male names, Ron and Ed

explanation.surface: Someone is under pressure to go along with a pair of men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressed' looks like 'urged', but it is creased clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressed clothes have been smoothed with a hot iron, so they are ironed.

clue.text: Cousin, 4, to report about

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to relate events is to report them
four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A cousin, the fourth one, is going to file a report on something.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but it is just the number in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is one example of a relative, a family member.

clue.text: Former British possession in New York state

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the British ..., now gone
second meaning: the state's nickname is the ... State

explanation.surface: A colony once held by Britain lay in what is now New York.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Empire was the realm Britain once held, and New York is nicknamed the Empire State.

clue.text: A group of directors on a cruise?

parts.note: taken as written
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: A company's directors take a holiday together on a cruise ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is an example: being on a cruise is one way of being on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers on a cruise ship are aboard, carried on the vessel.

clue.text: Couple I came across going the other way

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: travelling in the opposite direction means these letters are read right to left

parts.note: to come across someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: Someone passed a pair heading in the opposite direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people romantically linked are called an item, an informal term for a couple.

clue.text: One hands in very skilful lab work

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the following word

parts.note: an expert is highly skilled
I is the Roman numeral one
hands are workers, men

explanation.surface: Someone passes highly accomplished work done in a laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' reads as a verb, but it is the noun for workers, as in farm hands.
explanation.definitionFit: An experiment is the typical activity carried out in a laboratory.

clue.text: Fierce type in endless pain seen by doctor

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: the usual abbreviation
agony is great pain

explanation.surface: A ferocious patient in terrible pain is examined by a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is informally a fierce, intimidating person, often a stern woman.

clue.text: Eco-friendly accommodation, but no one would live in it

definitions.text: Eco-friendly accommodation, but no one would live in it

parts.note: surface reading: an environmentally sound home

parts.words: but no one would live in it
parts.note: setter's reading: a glass building for plants, not people

explanation.surface: A sustainable home that nobody actually wants to occupy.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as green (eco-friendly) plus house (accommodation), then see it is the gardener's glasshouse, where only plants live.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhouse is a glazed structure for growing plants, literally a green house yet unfit for people.

clue.text: Is adored to bits? That's by the way

indicators.note: smashed to bits, the letters fall apart and reassemble differently

parts.note: both words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are loved to pieces, then adds an offhand aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' looks like a conversational aside, but read literally it means beside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Something roadside stands next to the road, and a way is a road.

clue.text: Daybreak in Madrid

parts.note: surface reading: dawn, sunrise
setter's reading: a break taken during the day in Spain

explanation.surface: Dawn breaking over the Spanish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Daybreak means dawn, but split it as a break in the day: the Spanish afternoon rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is the traditional Spanish nap after lunch, a pause in the middle of the day.

clue.text: In navel diamond perhaps falling

parts.note: the navel sits in the tum, informal for belly
bling is showy jewellery, a diamond being an example

explanation.surface: A diamond worn as a belly-button piercing is dropping out.
explanation.walkthrough: TUM is a homely British word for stomach; the navel is on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbling means falling over and over, toppling down.

clue.text: Supporting one's bottom

explanation.surface: Holding up your own backside.
explanation.definitionFit: To be behind someone is to support them, and a behind is a polite word for the buttocks.

clue.text: Calamity as Diana succeeded Daisy

parts.note: a short form of the name
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Disaster strikes when Diana takes over from Daisy.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a calamity, a sudden event causing great damage.

clue.text: Goes sneakily about lifting cutlery

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: spoons are cutlery

explanation.surface: A thief creeps around pocketing the silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifting' suggests stealing, which suits the sneaking, but it signals reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To snoop is to pry or creep about furtively looking for information.

clue.text: Daring chap to stand in for principal?

definitions.text: Daring chap to stand in for principal?

parts.note: surface reading: a brave man covering for a headteacher
setter's reading: the principal is the lead actor, doubled in risky film scenes

explanation.surface: Someone bold enough to replace the head of a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' sounds like a school head, but in theatre and film it is the leading actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuntman performs dangerous action scenes in place of the star actor.

clue.text: Travel card: one's told to validate it

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the sound counts

parts.note: to tick something is to mark it as checked or valid

explanation.surface: A passenger is instructed to get their travel pass stamped.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket is the card or slip that entitles you to travel.

clue.text: Vehicle is hot — it does this in a puff of smoke?

definitions.text: it does this in a puff of smoke?
definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the verb answer

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
taken as written
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An overheated van disappears in a cloud of smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes what the vehicle does, which is the answer as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician's subject disappears in a puff of smoke, so it vanishes.

clue.text: Virginia, girl brought up as dependant

parts.note: the US state abbreviation

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl raised in Virginia as someone's ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' reads as raised, but it marks the girl word read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A vassal was a feudal subordinate who held land from a lord, hence a dependant.

clue.text: Young lads sharing a house perhaps, hopefully in good form

definitions.text: Young lads sharing a house perhaps, hopefully in good form

parts.words: Young lads sharing a house perhaps
parts.note: surface reading: boys living together in a flat
setter's reading: house and form are school groupings, so the boys are pupils

explanation.surface: Young men in a house share, hoping they are fit and well.
explanation.walkthrough: British schools divide pupils into houses and classes called forms, so 'house' and 'form' both point to school.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoolboys are boys at school, placed in a house and in a form or class.

clue.text: Batter bowled: timber!

parts.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
ash is a kind of timber

explanation.surface: A cricket batsman is out bowled and the umpire calls 'timber'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batter' and 'bowled' suggest cricket, but batter is the verb to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: To batter something is to bash it, striking it hard and repeatedly.

clue.text: Get very hot regularly in Black Sea

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Sweltering on the shores of the Black Sea in summer.
explanation.definitionFit: To bake informally means to be extremely hot, as in sweltering sun.

clue.text: Add spices in due time

explanation.surface: Put the seasoning in when the moment comes.
explanation.definitionFit: To season food is to flavour it, and a season is the appointed period for something.

clue.text: One animated little firework

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a lively, vivacious person
second meaning: a hand-held firework that throws sparks

explanation.surface: A small firework that seems to come alive.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparkler is both a sparkling, lively person and a small hand-held firework.
